entries.title: Normal or Hard difficulty
entries.before: One campaign ruleset.
entries.after: Choose Normal or Hard when starting a game. Hard adds level caps, Set battles and restrictions on Bag use.

entries.title: Original or Enhanced typings
entries.before: Species use their Gen 2 typings.
entries.after: Choose modern main-game typings or Crimson Crystal’s redesigned typings. This is independent of the stat choice.

entries.title: Original or Enhanced base stats
entries.before: Species use their Gen 2 base stats.
entries.after: Original uses modern main-game base stats. Enhanced uses Crimson Crystal’s balance changes.

entries.title: Abilities on or off
entries.before: Pokémon have no abilities.
entries.after: Choose whether abilities are enabled when starting a game. With abilities off, ability effects are disabled and Elm does not give the Ability Cap.

entries.title: Hard Mode forces Set battles
entries.before: Shift or Set can be selected.
entries.after: Hard Mode removes the free switch prompt after an opposing Pokémon faints. Normal retains the battle-style option.

entries.title: Hard Mode limits Bag use in battle
entries.before: Battle items can be used from the Bag.
entries.after: Only Ball-pocket items can be used from the battle Bag in Hard Mode. Healing items remain usable outside battle; held items still work.

entries.title: Hard Mode level caps
entries.before: No badge-based player level cap.
entries.after: The main challenge requires all 16 badges: Johto, then Kanto, then the League. Johto caps are 10, 16, 20, 25, 30, 34, 38 and 45. Kanto caps are 50, 54, 58, 62, 62, 62, 66 and 69. Earning Blue’s Earth Badge as the sixteenth badge removes progression-based level caps. The Elite Four, gym rematches and Mt. Silver have no progression cap.

entries.title: Hard Mode experience bonus
entries.before: Trainer battles award 1.5× base experience.
entries.after: Hard Mode trainer battles award 2× base experience. Badge-based level caps apply until Blue awards the sixteenth badge, then leveling is unrestricted by progression. Normal keeps the 1.5× trainer bonus.

entries.title: Hard Mode opponent training
entries.before: Trainer stats do not use this class-based training system.
entries.after: Trainer classes receive tailored stat experience in Hard Mode. Major opponents receive more training than ordinary route trainers; Normal uses zero trainer stat experience.

entries.title: Physical / special split
entries.before: A damaging move’s category is determined by its type.
entries.after: Each move has its own physical or special category. Physical moves use Attack and Defense; special moves use Special Attack and Special Defense.

entries.title: Critical-hit damage
entries.before: Critical hits deal roughly double damage.
entries.after: The critical-hit damage multiplier is 1.5×.

entries.title: Critical-hit rates
entries.before: The base critical-hit rate is about 1/16.
entries.after: The base rate is about 1/24; +1 stage is 1/8, +2 stages is 1/2, and +3 or more guarantees a critical hit.

entries.title: Focus Energy critical stages
entries.before: Focus Energy adds one critical stage.
entries.after: Focus Energy adds two critical stages. High-critical-hit moves add one stage; abilities and held items can add more.

entries.title: Damage variation
entries.before: Ordinary damage rolls span approximately 85% to 100%.
entries.after: Damage varies from about 85% to 100% on each hit.

entries.title: Enemy stat-lowering moves
entries.before: Enemy stat drops can suffer an additional random failure.
entries.after: Stat-lowering moves no longer have Gen 2’s extra 25% failure chance against the player.

entries.title: End-of-turn effect order
entries.before: Residual effects use the older turn flow.
entries.after: End-of-turn effects resolve by Speed within each phase. Trick Room reverses this order.

entries.title: Modern priority moves
entries.before: Priority uses the original move set.
entries.after: New moves and abilities have their own priority. Extreme Speed has +2 priority, Prankster adds +1 to status moves, and Triage adds +3 to supported healing moves.

entries.title: Freeze becomes frostbite
entries.before: Freeze prevents the Pokémon from acting.
entries.after: Frostbite halves Special Attack and deals 1/8 maximum HP damage each turn. The Pokémon can still act.

entries.title: Frostbite persists until cured
entries.before: Frozen Pokémon can thaw naturally.
entries.after: Frostbite does not thaw at random. Using the Pokémon’s own Fire moves does not cure it.

entries.title: Frostbite protection and healing
entries.before: Ice typing and anti-freeze effects protect against freeze.
entries.after: Ice Heal, Ice Berry and full-status cures remove frostbite. Magma Armor prevents or cures it, and harsh sunlight prevents moves from inflicting it.

entries.title: Burn damage
entries.before: Burn deals 1/8 maximum HP each turn.
entries.after: Burn deals 1/16 maximum HP each turn and still halves Attack, subject to abilities such as Guts.

entries.title: Paralysis Speed reduction
entries.before: Paralysis reduces Speed to one quarter.
entries.after: Paralysis halves Speed. Its 25% chance to prevent an action remains.

entries.title: Electric types resist paralysis
entries.before: Electric typing does not provide blanket paralysis immunity.
entries.after: Electric-type Pokémon cannot be paralyzed, including by non-Electric moves or secondary effects.

entries.title: Grass types block powder moves
entries.before: Grass typing does not block powders.
entries.after: Grass types are immune to Poison Powder, Stun Spore, Sleep Powder, Spore and Cotton Spore.

entries.title: Powder immunity cannot be bypassed
entries.before: There is no Grass powder immunity.
entries.after: No Guard and Mold Breaker cannot bypass Grass types’ powder immunity.

entries.title: Powder Snow is still an attack
entries.before: Powder Snow is a damaging Ice move.
entries.after: Powder Snow remains a damaging Ice move and is not blocked by Grass powder immunity.

entries.title: Effect Spore and Grass typing
entries.before: Abilities do not exist.
entries.after: Grass types are also protected from Effect Spore’s contact-triggered status.

entries.title: Ghost types escape trapping
entries.before: Ghost typing does not exempt a Pokémon from trapping.
entries.after: Ghost types can leave trapping effects and trapping abilities.

entries.title: Sleep duration
entries.before: Ordinary inflicted sleep uses the older 2–7 turn roll.
entries.after: Ordinary sleep uses a 1–3 turn duration. Rest retains its own fixed sleep duration, and abilities can modify waking.

entries.title: Confusion
entries.before: Confusion has a 50% self-hit chance.
entries.after: Confused Pokémon have a 50% chance to hit themselves.

entries.title: Overworld poison can still cause fainting
entries.before: Poison damages the party while walking and can cause fainting.
entries.after: Poison damages Pokémon while walking and can knock them out.

entries.title: Viridian Forest rain and restless trees
entries.before: Viridian Forest does not have its own daily rain or animated forest trees.
entries.after: Viridian Forest keeps its custom green palette throughout the day and night. Each day has a 50% chance of rain, remembered when you leave and return. During rain, its large trees sway with the Celebi-style animation.

entries.title: Hail weather
entries.before: Hail does not exist.
entries.after: Hail deals 1/16 maximum HP damage each turn to non-Ice Pokémon unless an ability protects them. Blizzard always hits in hail.

entries.title: Hail also boosts Ice Defense
entries.before: No hail or snow Defense boost.
entries.after: Ice types gain 50% Defense during hail.

entries.title: Sandstorm boosts Rock Special Defense
entries.before: Sandstorm does not boost Rock-type Special Defense.
entries.after: Rock types receive a 1.5× Special Defense boost against special moves during sandstorm.

entries.title: Weather lasts five or eight turns
entries.before: Weather moves use the original duration rules.
entries.after: Weather moves and weather abilities set five turns of weather, extended to eight by the matching weather rock.

entries.title: Weather suppression
entries.before: No ability-based weather suppression.
entries.after: Cloud Nine suppresses weather effects while its active holder is alive. The underlying weather remains and resumes when suppression ends.

entries.title: Trick Room
entries.before: Trick Room does not exist.
entries.after: Trick Room reverses ordinary Speed order for five turns. Using it again ends it early; priority still matters.

entries.title: Three ability slots
entries.before: Pokémon have no abilities.
entries.after: Pokémon can have up to three abilities, labeled Ability 1, Ability 2 and Ability 3. Each Pokémon page lists its available slots. Use the reusable Ability Cap to freely swap between them.

entries.title: Ability activation banners
entries.before: Pokémon have no abilities.
entries.after: Battle banners show which Pokémon and ability activated.

entries.title: Reusable Ability Cap
entries.before: There is no ability-changing item.
entries.after: Use Elm’s reusable Ability Cap to freely cycle through a Pokémon’s available Ability 1, Ability 2 and Ability 3 slots.

entries.title: Modern Sturdy
entries.before: Abilities do not exist.
entries.after: At full HP, Sturdy allows its holder to survive a damaging hit with 1 HP. It also protects against one-hit KO moves.

entries.title: Gale Wings has no full-HP restriction
entries.before: Abilities do not exist.
entries.after: Gale Wings gives Flying moves +1 priority at any HP.

entries.title: Disguise uses its original no-chip version
entries.before: Abilities do not exist.
entries.after: Disguise blocks the first damaging hit without costing HP.

entries.title: Parental Bond follow-up hit
entries.before: Abilities do not exist.
entries.after: Eligible attacks hit twice. The second hit deals one quarter of normal damage.

entries.title: Mega Sol is a custom ability
entries.before: Abilities do not exist.
entries.after: The holder uses supported moves as though harsh sunlight were active, including Solar Beam, Weather Ball, recovery and damage adjustments. It does not set field weather for both sides.

entries.title: Supreme Overlord scales with fallen allies
entries.before: Abilities do not exist.
entries.after: Damage increases by 10% for each fainted non-Egg ally, up to five allies and a 1.5× multiplier.

entries.title: Palafin has no Zero to Hero transformation
entries.before: Palafin does not exist.
entries.after: Palafin stays in its base form and does not transform into Hero Form.

entries.title: Hyper Beam and Giga Impact skip recharge after a KO
entries.before: Hyper Beam still requires recharge after knocking out its target.
entries.after: Hyper Beam and Giga Impact end without recharge when they knock out the target, following the Gen 1-style rule. A surviving target still causes recharge.

entries.title: Hidden Power has a selectable type
entries.before: Hidden Power’s type is determined by DVs.
entries.after: Choose each Pokémon’s Hidden Power type at the house northwest of the Lake of Rage. Untuned Pokémon default to Dark; DVs do not determine the type.

entries.title: Hidden Power has fixed power
entries.before: Hidden Power’s power varies with DVs.
entries.after: Hidden Power has 70 base power.

entries.title: Hidden Power chooses its category dynamically
entries.before: Hidden Power’s damage category follows its type.
entries.after: It becomes physical when the user’s current Attack exceeds Special Attack, and special otherwise. Stat-stage changes are considered; ties use special.

entries.title: Octazooka lowers both defenses
entries.before: Octazooka has 65 power, 85% accuracy and a chance to lower accuracy.
entries.after: Octazooka has 90 power, 100% accuracy and a 20% chance to lower Defense and Special Defense together by one stage.

entries.title: Incinerate has custom power
entries.before: Incinerate does not exist.
entries.after: Incinerate has 75 power and destroys a removable held Berry after a successful hit.

entries.title: Low Kick
entries.before: Low Kick has fixed 50 power and can flinch.
entries.after: Low Kick has 50 power, 100% accuracy and a 30% flinch chance.

entries.title: Teleport retains escape behavior
entries.before: Teleport attempts to escape wild battles and fails in trainer battles.
entries.after: Teleport escapes wild battles. It cannot switch Pokémon in trainer battles.

entries.title: Giga Hammer and Blood Moon have a repeat-use lock
entries.before: These moves do not exist.
entries.after: Giga Hammer and Blood Moon cannot be used on consecutive turns. If you select one again, you can choose another move.

entries.title: Explosion and Selfdestruct use normal Defense
entries.before: These moves halve the target’s Defense during damage calculation.
entries.after: Explosion and Selfdestruct no longer halve Defense.

entries.title: Protect becomes harder to repeat
entries.before: Repeated Protect halves the next success chance.
entries.after: Repeated Protect uses approximately 1/3, 1/9, 1/27 and so on. A different action resets the chain.

entries.title: Spikes stack in three layers
entries.before: Spikes has one layer and deals 1/8 maximum HP.
entries.after: Spikes stacks up to three layers: 1/8, 1/6 and 1/4 maximum HP entry damage. Flying types and other ungrounded Pokémon avoid it.

entries.title: Stealth Rock
entries.before: Stealth Rock does not exist.
entries.after: Entering Pokémon take Rock-type effectiveness-scaled damage, normally 1/8 maximum HP at neutral effectiveness.

entries.title: Toxic Spikes
entries.before: Toxic Spikes does not exist.
entries.after: One layer poisons grounded entrants; two layers badly poison them. Grounded Poison types remove the layers.

entries.title: Sticky Web
entries.before: Sticky Web does not exist.
entries.after: Lowers grounded opponents’ Speed by one stage when they enter battle.

entries.title: Spider Web
entries.before: Traps the target, preventing switching and fleeing.
entries.after: Sets an entry hazard that poisons grounded opponents and lowers their Speed by one stage. Poison types do not absorb it. It can stack with Sticky Web, and Rapid Spin, Mortal Spin or Defog removes it.

entries.title: Rapid Spin clears all supported hazards
entries.before: Rapid Spin clears Gen 2 Spikes, trapping and Leech Seed.
entries.after: Rapid Spin removes Spikes, Toxic Spikes, Stealth Rock, Sticky Web and Spider Web from the user’s side.

entries.title: Defog clears hazards and screens
entries.before: Defog does not exist.
entries.after: Defog removes hazards from both sides and removes Reflect and Light Screen from the target’s side.

entries.title: Wish heals the active slot next turn
entries.before: Wish does not exist.
entries.after: At the end of the following turn, Wish heals the active Pokémon on the user’s side for half of the original user’s maximum HP. It can heal a teammate switched into that slot.

entries.title: Taunt
entries.before: Taunt does not exist.
entries.after: Taunt blocks status moves for three turns. Oblivious protects against it.

entries.title: Torment
entries.before: Torment does not exist.
entries.after: Torment prevents consecutive use of the same move until the affected Pokémon leaves the field. Struggle remains legal.

entries.title: Yawn
entries.before: Yawn does not exist.
entries.after: Yawn makes the target fall asleep at the end of the next turn if it remains eligible.

entries.title: Knock Off bonus damage
entries.before: Knock Off does not exist.
entries.after: Knock Off deals 1.5× damage when the target has a removable item, then removes it when permitted.

entries.title: Weather Ball changes in battle
entries.before: Weather Ball does not exist.
entries.after: Weather Ball is normally a 50-power Normal move. Active weather changes its type and doubles its base power; suppressed weather does not apply.

entries.title: Sound moves bypass Substitute
entries.before: Sound moves do not have this general Substitute bypass.
entries.after: Sound moves bypass Substitute. Infiltrator also lets attacks bypass Substitute.

entries.title: Sucker Punch checks the opponent’s action
entries.before: Sucker Punch does not exist.
entries.after: It succeeds only before the opponent acts and when they have selected a damaging move. Switching, using an item, recharging or choosing a status move makes it fail.

entries.title: Expanded evolution methods
entries.before: Only the original evolution chains and items are present.
entries.after: Added Pokémon use new evolution items and methods. Each Pokémon page lists its evolution requirements.

entries.title: Slugma evolves sooner
entries.before: Slugma evolves into Magcargo at level 38.
entries.after: Slugma evolves into Magcargo at level 34.

entries.title: Low-health alarm stops after three beeps
entries.before: The red-HP alarm repeats continuously.
entries.after: The low-HP alarm stops after three beeps. It resets when the Pokémon leaves red HP.

entries.title: Day-Care Eggs
entries.before: A random initial countdown and repeated compatibility-dependent rolls can require a long walk before an egg appears.
entries.after: Compatible parents produce an Egg after 64 steps. Collect it before they can produce another.

entries.title: Faster Egg hatching
entries.before: Eggs take 256 steps per hatch cycle.
entries.after: Eggs hatch sixteen times faster. Magikarp takes up to 80 steps and Eevee up to 560.

entries.title: Reusable TMs
entries.before: A TM is consumed when used.
entries.after: TMs are reusable.

entries.title: Updated level-up learnsets
entries.before: The original Crystal learnsets are used.
entries.after: Pokémon have revised level-up moves and TM compatibility.

entries.title: Move Reminder
entries.before: Crystal has no Move Reminder.
entries.after: The Move Reminder in Blackthorn’s Move Deleter House charges ₽1,000 to reteach level-up moves from a Pokémon’s evolution line, up to its current level.

entries.title: Modern breeding move inheritance
entries.before: Only the father passes egg moves, and compatible TM/HM moves can be inherited.
entries.after: Either parent can pass down egg moves. Other level-up moves pass down when both parents know them. TM compatibility alone does not pass down moves, and Ditto does not pass down moves. If more than four moves qualify, egg moves take priority.

entries.title: Family / egg-move tutor
entries.before: Egg moves require breeding.
entries.after: The purple tutor in the Move Deleter’s house teaches compatible family/egg moves for ¥5,000 per successful lesson.

entries.title: Goldenrod utility tutor
entries.before: There is no utility tutor.
entries.after: The PP speech house in Goldenrod has a tutor for Substitute, Sleep Talk, Reflect, Light Screen and Thunder Wave, according to compatibility. Successful lessons cost ¥1,000.

entries.title: Meowth and Persian learn Fake Out
entries.before: Fake Out does not exist.
entries.after: Meowth and Persian have Fake Out at level 1, including through the Move Reminder when eligible.

entries.title: Lickilicky learns Wish
entries.before: Lickilicky and Wish do not exist.
entries.after: Lickilicky learns Wish at level 50.

entries.title: DVs and stat experience
entries.before: Gen 2 uses DVs and stat experience.
entries.after: Pokémon use Gen 2 DVs and stat experience. Natures, modern IVs and the 510-EV limit are not used.

entries.title: Shiny odds are about 2%
entries.before: Ordinary shiny odds are 1/8,192 and depend on DVs.
entries.after: Wild, gifted and hatched Pokémon have about a 2% shiny chance (5/256), independent of their DVs.

entries.title: Clone starters are an exception to random shininess
entries.before: Clone starter forms do not exist.
entries.after: Clone starters cannot be randomly shiny.

entries.title: Choice Band
entries.before: Choice Band does not exist.
entries.after: Boosts Attack by 50% and locks the holder into its chosen move until switching.

entries.title: Choice Specs
entries.before: Choice Specs does not exist.
entries.after: Boosts Special Attack by 50% and locks the holder into its chosen move until switching.

entries.title: Choice Scarf
entries.before: Choice Scarf does not exist.
entries.after: Boosts Speed by 50% and locks the holder into its chosen move until switching.

entries.title: Eviolite
entries.before: Eviolite does not exist.
entries.after: Boosts Defense and Special Defense by 50% for species that can still evolve.

entries.title: Assault Vest
entries.before: Assault Vest does not exist.
entries.after: Boosts Special Defense by 50% while preventing the holder from selecting status moves.

entries.title: Focus Sash
entries.before: Focus Sash does not exist.
entries.after: At full HP, a consumable Focus Sash lets its holder survive a damaging hit with 1 HP.

entries.title: Expert Belt
entries.before: Expert Belt does not exist.
entries.after: Boosts super-effective move damage by 20%.

entries.title: Life Orb
entries.before: Life Orb does not exist.
entries.after: Boosts move damage by 30%, with recoil after a successful damaging move unless prevented.

entries.title: Rocky Helmet
entries.before: Rocky Helmet does not exist.
entries.after: Contact attackers lose 1/6 of their maximum HP.

entries.title: Weakness Policy
entries.before: Weakness Policy does not exist.
entries.after: When a super-effective damaging hit activates it, this consumable item raises Attack and Special Attack by two stages.

entries.title: Loaded Dice
entries.before: Loaded Dice does not exist.
entries.after: Multi-hit moves usually strike four or five times. Loaded Dice also improves Triple Kick and Triple Axel’s repeated accuracy checks.

entries.title: Flame Orb
entries.before: Flame Orb does not exist.
entries.after: Burns the holder at the end of the turn if it can be burned.

entries.title: Toxic Orb
entries.before: Toxic Orb does not exist.
entries.after: Badly poisons the holder at the end of the turn if it can be poisoned.

entries.title: Damp Rock
entries.before: Damp Rock does not exist.
entries.after: Extends rain summoned by its holder from five to eight turns.

entries.title: Heat Rock
entries.before: Heat Rock does not exist.
entries.after: Extends harsh sunlight summoned by its holder from five to eight turns.

entries.title: Smooth Rock
entries.before: Smooth Rock does not exist.
entries.after: Extends sandstorm summoned by its holder from five to eight turns.

entries.title: Icy Rock
entries.before: Icy Rock does not exist.
entries.after: Extends hail summoned by its holder from five to eight turns.

entries.title: Larger item pocket
entries.before: The item pocket holds 20 distinct stacks.
entries.after: The item pocket holds 40 distinct stacks. The Ball pocket holds 12.

entries.title: More Pokémon storage
entries.before: Crystal has 14 boxes of 20 Pokémon.
entries.after: Store up to 500 Pokémon in 25 boxes.

entries.title: Graphical PC storage
entries.before: Bill’s PC uses the original text-list interface.
entries.after: Move Pokémon and held items, rename boxes and choose box themes in the PC storage interface.

entries.title: Use another Repel prompt
entries.before: When Repel expires, the player must reopen the Bag.
entries.after: When a Repel wears off, you can use another without opening the Bag. The prompt offers the same type if available, then Max Repel, Super Repel or Repel.

entries.title: Repeat-use consumables
entries.before: Using a party consumable returns to the Bag after each use.
entries.after: Use healing items, vitamins, PP items and Rare Candies on multiple Pokémon without reopening the Bag after each use.

entries.title: Apricorn trees give three
entries.before: Apricorn trees give one Apricorn per harvest.
entries.after: Apricorn trees give three per harvest. Ordinary fruit trees still give one item.

entries.title: New evolution items
entries.before: The original evolution-item set is used.
entries.after: Dusk Stone, Ice Stone and evolution apples support the expanded evolution chains. The Pokémon pages show which item each species needs.

entries.title: Fossil revival
entries.before: Crystal has no usable fossil-revival service.
entries.after: Bring fossils to the Ruins of Alph Fossil Lab to revive them.

entries.title: Expanded Pokémon roster
entries.before: Crystal has 251 species.
entries.after: The roster includes later-generation Pokémon, regional forms, custom species and nine clone starters.

entries.title: Regional forms
entries.before: Regional forms do not exist.
entries.after: Alolan, Galarian, Hisuian and Paldean forms have their own abilities, typings, stats and evolutions.

entries.title: Custom Pokémon
entries.before: These species are absent.
entries.after: Custom Pokémon include Mesmeria, Kotora, Raitora, Gorotora, Watu and Gorochu, plus Bloodmoon pre-evolutions.

entries.title: Four playable trainers
entries.before: Crystal offers two player characters.
entries.after: Choose Gold, Lyra, Indigo or Mint as your player character.

entries.title: Bicycle or skateboard
entries.before: Goldenrod’s shop lends a Bicycle.
entries.after: Choose a Bicycle or Skateboard at the Goldenrod Bike Shop. You can only claim one.

entries.title: Daily regional overworld weather
entries.before: There is no broad daily regional weather system.
entries.after: Johto and Kanto areas receive daily weather, including overcast skies, rain, thunderstorms and harsh sunlight. Neighboring maps share regional selections.

entries.title: Overworld weather affects battles
entries.before: Outdoor map weather does not generally seed battles.
entries.after: Applicable regional rain, harsh sun, snow/hail and sandstorm can carry into battles. Plain sunny skies do not automatically mean battle harsh sunlight.

entries.title: Safari Zone is playable
entries.before: Crystal’s Safari Zone is closed.
entries.after: Pay ₽500 to enter the Safari Zone with 30 Safari Balls and 300 steps.

entries.title: Bug-Catching Contest overhaul
entries.before: The original Contest rules and judging are used.
entries.after: The Bug-Catching Contest has new Pokémon and revised scoring.

entries.title: Silent Crypt
entries.before: This area and its gravekeeping quest are absent.
entries.after: Silent Crypt adds Ghost-focused encounters, trainers and a gravekeeping quest near Route 37.

entries.title: Ice Island
entries.before: This area is absent.
entries.after: Ice Island is reachable from Route 19 and includes an Articuno encounter.

entries.title: Expanded wild encounter pools
entries.before: Wild encounters use the original roster.
entries.after: Find new Pokémon through grass, Surf, fishing, Headbutt, Rock Smash, swarms and special encounters.

entries.title: Rebalanced trainers and rematches
entries.before: Crystal’s original trainer parties and progression are used.
entries.after: Trainers, rivals, gym leaders and rematch opponents have revised teams.

entries.title: Sixteen badges before the League
entries.before: The League follows Johto's eight gyms, with Kanto explored afterwards.
entries.after: Collect all 16 badges before challenging the Elite Four. Blue returns to Viridian Gym after you speak to him on Cinnabar with 15 badges. The southern Kanto routes open after defeating Erika, Sabrina and Janine. After winning the League, begin the Johto gym rematches with Falkner.

entries.title: Tower wings after eight Johto badges
entries.before: The Silver Wing is available on reaching Pewter, while the Rainbow Wing requires a League victory and the three legendary beasts.
entries.after: Collect all eight Johto badges to receive the Silver Wing from Pewter’s old man. For the Rainbow Wing, also catch Raikou, Entei and Suicune yourself, then speak to the Tin Tower sage. The beasts can be in your party or PC. Lugia and Ho-Oh are level 60.

entries.title: Crystal’s story and Mew encounter
entries.before: There is no added Crystal rival story or Route 25 Mew event.
entries.after: Crystal’s story continues through new encounters and a Mew event at Cerulean Cape.

entries.title: Pallet Town superboss encounter
entries.before: Red’s main encounter is at Mt. Silver.
entries.after: A later story event unlocks a Red battle in Pallet Town.

entries.title: Trainer dialogue portraits
entries.before: Dialogue uses the original text presentation.
entries.after: Major characters have illustrated dialogue portraits.

entries.title: Updated Pokémon artwork and animations
entries.before: Original Crystal graphics are used.
entries.after: Pokémon have updated sprites, icons, cries and animations.

entries.title: Updated maps and water graphics
entries.before: Original map artwork is used.
entries.after: Towns, routes, new areas, water tiles and overworld objects have revised artwork and layouts.

entries.title: Fairy type
entries.before: Gen 2 has no Fairy type.
entries.after: Fairy is immune to Dragon, weak to Poison and Steel, and super effective against Fighting, Dragon and Dark.

entries.title: Steel no longer resists Ghost or Dark
entries.before: Steel resists Ghost and Dark.
entries.after: Ghost and Dark attacks deal neutral damage to Steel before any second type is considered.

entries.title: Critical hits ignore unfavorable stat stages
entries.before: Gen 2 checks Attack and Defense stage relationships together.
entries.after: Critical hits ignore the attacker’s negative offensive stages and the defender’s positive defensive stages independently. Favorable offensive stages and lowered defenses still help.

entries.title: Dark types block opposing Prankster status moves
entries.before: Abilities do not exist.
entries.after: Dark types are immune to opposing status moves boosted by Prankster. The user can still use Prankster moves targeting itself or its own side.

entries.title: Bad poison persists through switching
entries.before: Switching converts bad poison into regular poison.
entries.after: A badly poisoned Pokémon remains badly poisoned after switching. Its escalating damage counter resets when it re-enters battle.

entries.title: Disable has a fixed duration
entries.before: Disable uses a variable duration.
entries.after: Disable lasts four turns.

entries.title: Encore has a fixed duration
entries.before: Encore uses a variable duration.
entries.after: Encore lasts three turns.

entries.title: Endure shares the Protect chain
entries.before: Endure uses the older consecutive-use odds.
entries.after: Endure shares Protect’s consecutive-use success system, including the progressively reduced chance.

entries.title: Bide releases on turn three
entries.before: Bide’s storing period can vary.
entries.after: Bide stores damage on its first two turns and releases on turn three. Its retaliation ignores type immunity.

entries.title: Struggle uses maximum-HP recoil
entries.before: Struggle recoil is based on the damage dealt.
entries.after: Struggle recoil is one quarter of the user’s maximum HP. Rock Head and Magic Guard do not prevent this recoil.

entries.title: Rapid Spin does not raise Speed
entries.before: Rapid Spin has no Speed boost.
entries.after: Rapid Spin has 50 power and does not raise Speed.

entries.title: Growth
entries.before: Growth raises Special Attack by one stage.
entries.after: Growth raises Special Attack by one stage.

entries.title: Thunder Wave
entries.before: Thunder Wave has 100% accuracy.
entries.after: Thunder Wave has 100% accuracy. Ground types and Electric types are immune.

entries.title: Flash Fire raises the higher offensive stat
entries.before: Abilities do not exist.
entries.after: Absorbing a Fire move raises the holder’s higher Attack or Special Attack by one stage. Ties raise Special Attack. The boosts can stack.

entries.title: Air Balloon
entries.before: Air Balloon does not exist.
entries.after: The holder avoids Ground attacks and grounded entry hazards until a damaging hit pops the balloon.

entries.title: Muscle Band
entries.before: Muscle Band does not exist.
entries.after: Boosts physical move damage by 10%.

entries.title: Wise Glasses
entries.before: Wise Glasses do not exist.
entries.after: Boosts special move damage by 10%.

entries.title: Light Ball boosts both offensive stats
entries.before: Light Ball doubles Pikachu’s Special Attack.
entries.after: Light Ball doubles Pikachu’s Attack and Special Attack.

entries.title: Focus Band has an increased chance
entries.before: Focus Band has roughly a 10% activation chance.
entries.after: Focus Band has roughly a 30% chance to let its holder survive a knockout with 1 HP, at any starting HP.

entries.title: Relic Clock
entries.before: This key item does not exist.
entries.after: Find the Relic Clock in Ilex Forest to reset the game clock.

entries.title: Most acquired Pokémon receive perfect DVs
entries.before: DVs normally vary between individual Pokémon.
entries.after: Most caught, gifted and hatched Pokémon have perfect DVs.

entries.title: Unown and Magikarp keep wild DVs
entries.before: Unown letters and Magikarp length depend on their DVs.
entries.after: Wild Unown and Magikarp have random DVs, allowing different Unown letters and Magikarp lengths.

entries.title: Badge battle bonuses removed
entries.before: Johto badges increase particular player battle stats, and both regions' badges boost damage for their corresponding move types.
entries.after: Badges no longer boost battle stats or move damage.

entries.title: Overworld weather in battle
entries.before: No broad overworld-to-battle weather transfer.
entries.after: Overworld weather lasts throughout a battle until replaced by a weather move or ability.

entries.title: Safari Zone progression gate
entries.before: The Safari Zone is closed.
entries.after: Five Johto badges unlock stronger Safari encounters, including Kangaskhan, Paldean Tauros and Skarmory.

entries.title: Bug-Catching Contest scoring
entries.before: Judging uses the original Crystal scoring formula.
entries.after: Bug-Catching Contest scores depend on species rarity, level and how few Park Balls you used to catch the Pokémon.

entries.title: Viridian Forest is restored
entries.before: Crystal compresses the forest into Route 2.
entries.after: Explore Viridian Forest and its new encounters in Kanto.

entries.title: Fire Island
entries.before: This area is absent.
entries.after: Visit Fire Island from Route 19 to encounter Moltres.

entries.title: Thunder Island
entries.before: This area is absent.
entries.after: Visit Thunder Island from Route 19 to encounter Zapdos.

entries.title: Elemental Sphere opens the bird islands
entries.before: This quest item and island-opening event are absent.
entries.after: The Elemental Sphere obtained in Lugia’s chamber can be placed at Route 19 to open Fire Island, Thunder Island and Ice Island.

entries.title: Type-boosting items
entries.before: Held type-boosting items generally add 10% damage.
entries.after: Type-boosting items such as Charcoal, Mystic Water and Magnet increase damage by 10%.

entries.title: Thick Club supports Alolan Marowak
entries.before: Thick Club doubles Attack for Cubone and Marowak; Alolan forms are absent.
entries.after: Thick Club doubles Attack for Cubone, Marowak and Alolan Marowak.

entries.title: Metal Powder after transformation
entries.before: Metal Powder gives Ditto 50% more Defense and Special Defense, including after Transform.
entries.after: Metal Powder gives Ditto 50% more Defense and Special Defense, including after Transform or Imposter. Klutz disables the bonus.

entries.title: Refuse the Rocket toll
entries.before: The Route 43 gate Rockets automatically take ₽1,000, or all your remaining money, when you pass through.
entries.after: Pay the Route 43 Rockets ₽1,000 or refuse and fight both without healing between battles. Defeat both to remove the toll permanently.

entries.title: Meet Jasmine outside the lighthouse
entries.before: Jasmine requests and receives the SecretPotion on the lighthouse's top floor, then treats Amphy immediately.
entries.after: Meet Jasmine outside Olivine Lighthouse and bring her the SecretPotion from Cianwood. Then speak to her beside Amphy to heal him and reopen her Gym.

entries.title: Held items around the world
entries.before: The added battle items do not exist in original Crystal.
entries.after: Find battle items through exploration and side quests, including Eviolite at Day Care, Rocky Helmet from Anthony on Route 33 and Loaded Dice in Goldenrod Underground.

entries.title: Mahogany held-item shop
entries.before: Mahogany has only the original supply inventories.
entries.after: After clearing the Rocket Hideout, buy held items from the granny in Mahogany Mart. Stock includes Eviolite, Rocky Helmet, Air Balloon, Muscle Band, Wise Glasses, Expert Belt, Flame Orb, Toxic Orb, Assault Vest, Life Orb and Wide Lens.

entries.title: Choose Battle Tower gear prizes
entries.before: The Battle Tower awards a random vitamin after a seven-win streak.
entries.after: Win a seven-battle challenge to choose a Choice Band, Choice Specs, Choice Scarf, Focus Sash or Weakness Policy. Win more challenges for extra copies.

entries.title: Special item acquisition methods
entries.before: Some items rely on special activities, rare held items or Mystery Gift.
entries.after: Eon Mail comes from Mystery Gift. Steal BrightPowder from Koga’s or Janine’s Crobat. Find the four weather rocks in the Ho-Oh secret chamber at the Ruins of Alph.

entries.title: Doom Desire: immediate 160-power strike
entries.before: Delayed Steel attack in the mainline games.
entries.after: Doom Desire is a 160-power special Steel attack with 100% accuracy and 5 PP. It strikes immediately and cannot be used twice in succession, just like Giga Hammer. Using another move or switching out clears its reuse restriction.

entries.title: Lumi power buffs and accuracy changes
entries.before: Mainline move values.
entries.after: Dragon Hammer has 120 power; Blaze Kick and Poison Tail have 90. Meteor Mash and Sky Uppercut have 100% accuracy, and Blaze Kick has 95%. Sky Uppercut can hit opponents during Fly or Bounce.

entries.title: Tail Glow for Ampharos and Lanturn
entries.before: Tail Glow unavailable.
entries.after: Ampharos can relearn Tail Glow from its level-1 reminder slot. Lanturn learns it at level 40. Tail Glow raises Special Attack by three stages; Cotton Guard raises Defense by three, while Cosmic Power raises both defenses by one.

entries.title: Recycle recovers a consumed item
entries.before: Recycle unavailable.
entries.after: Recycle restores the user’s last consumed held item when it is empty-handed. That history survives switching during the same battle. Recovered items work with Harvest, Cud Chew, Klutz and Unburden; removed or destroyed items do not become new Recycle targets.

entries.title: Save format 4 and retained editor profiles
entries.before: The Jirachi/Wishing Star build uses save format 3; earlier builds use format 2.
entries.after: The current build uses format 4, with 498 species and 440 moves. The ROM automatically upgrades valid format-3 saves to add Phantump and Trevenant caught/seen flags while preserving map, event and Pokemon progress. The save editor includes both new species, their normal/shiny sprites, Horn Leech and all previous profiles. Format-2 saves can use the editor migration control with a new-ROM save template; map and event progress then comes from that template.

entries.title: Phantump and Trevenant
entries.before: The Phantump family is unavailable in original Crystal.
entries.after: Phantump and Trevenant are regional Pokedex #287 and #288, before the Duskull family. Find level-35 Phantump (10% slot) or level-36 Trevenant (1% slot) on Route 43 at night. Phantump evolves at level 32, and Trevenant is offered Shadow Claw on evolution. Both have Ghost/Grass typing and Natural Cure, Frisk or Harvest. Supported historical main-series moves through Scarlet/Violet are available via level-up, machines, breeding, the reminder and tutors; moves not implemented in this game remain excluded. Its level-32 evolution is a Crimson Crystal change.

entries.title: Horn Leech
entries.before: Horn Leech is unavailable in original Crystal.
entries.after: Horn Leech is a 75-power physical Grass contact move with 100% accuracy and 10 PP. It restores half the damage dealt, rounded up, and receives Triage priority. Phantump, Trevenant, Stantler and Wyrdeer learn it at level 28. Stantler and Wyrdeer receiving Horn Leech is a Crimson Crystal addition that applies to both Original and Enhanced rules. Its dedicated attack-and-drain animation is ported from Polished Coral.

entries.title: Low Kick, Grass Knot, Heavy Slam and Heat Crash use weight
entries.before: Low Kick has 50 power and may cause flinching. Grass Knot and Heavy Slam do not exist.
entries.after: These moves use each Pokémon’s Pokédex weight with the modern formulas. Low Kick and Grass Knot have 20, 40, 60, 80, 100 or 120 power against targets under 10 kg, from 10 kg, 25 kg, 50 kg, 100 kg and 200 kg. Heavy Slam and Heat Crash have 40 power, rising to 60, 80, 100 or 120 when the user weighs at least two, three, four or five times as much as the target. Heavy Slam and Heat Crash deal double damage to, and never miss, a target that used Minimize. A transformed Pokémon uses its new form’s weight. Low Kick no longer flinches, and Heat Crash no longer burns. Grass Knot is a special Grass contact move; Heavy Slam is a physical Steel contact move.

entries.title: Grass Knot and Heavy Slam learners
entries.before: Grass Knot and Heavy Slam are unavailable in original Crystal.
entries.after: Every Pokémon that can learn Grass Knot or Heavy Slam in the main series through Scarlet and Violet can learn it here. Aron, Lairon, Aggron, Golem, Snorlax, Forretress, Numel, Camerupt, Shieldon, Bastiodon, Golett and Golurk learn Heavy Slam by level-up; Onix and Phanpy can learn it as an Egg Move. The Blackthorn move tutor teaches the rest. Grass Knot’s animation comes from mae-pokeorange; Heavy Slam has a new animation: a Metal Claw-style steel sheen over the user, a forward lunge and a heavy impact.
